tpl.dashboard.title: Steering
tpl.dashboard.info.overview:
What it is for
Show at a glance where the project stands, end to end: what is approved, what waits for its gate, what is in progress, what comes next.
What it shows
The roadmap view reduced to its Deliverables row: one column per phase, then one per release; gates as vertical bars between the columns, green once passed. Each card leads to its deliverable. In a release column, three deliverables in a row: Development, Testing, Delivery. A Workstream analyses card is added to every column, phase or release, that at least one workstream prepares: last in the column, with the count of its workstreams; all lead to the inventory of the analyses.
Sprints
A release takes several sprints: each one is a numbered dot under the card (green: done, solid white: in progress). Only started sprints have a dot: the number of sprints to come is not known before their planning. The card leads to the current sprint (Development), the last campaign (Testing), the last acceptance report (Delivery); each dot leads to the page of its sprint, its campaign or its report, as soon as it exists.
States
To come (not started), in progress, produced and waiting for its gate, approved: the colours of the roadmap, plus "in progress". The small count ("7/13 stories") shows when it exists. No planned date and no delay: dates live in the roadmap schedule.
Release columns
A single "Release" column, with its G3 gate, as long as neither the story map nor the roadmap names the releases; once they do (MVP, release R2…), one column per release, each with its G3.
G3 of a release
Passed when every story of the release is accepted in a signed acceptance report, with or without reservations.
Current column
On a narrow screen, the grid scrolls in its frame and opens on the current column, marked by data-current on its header: the current phase, or the release of the current sprint.
Gates
Under the grid, one row per gate, from G0 to the G3 of each sprint of the release: date held, verdict, reservations, and the deliverable that records it; the next gate shows the end date of its sprint. Gates are the moments when the human commits the project, from G0 to each G3.
tpl.dashboard.info.hotspot:
What it is for
List the hotspots: what only the human can decide, so that they see it when opening the page, without waiting for the PO to bring it.
What it shows
A gate ready to present; business questions raised by the PO; high-impact open points of the detailed design; ADRs proposed with a deviation from the stack; stuck review loops (three correction rounds without convergence); plugin changes proposed by a retrospective; acceptance reservations still open (badge, severity of the linked defect, sprint of the report, what will lift it), a reservation being lifted when its linked item, defect BUG-xxx or ticket T-xxx, moves to status done. Each row names what is waiting, with what its files say about it, and since when it has been waiting.
Filter
One chip per type present, with its number of rows: a click turns it on or off, several chips add up; "All", or no active chip, shows everything. The filter is not kept from one visit to the next: a new type must never be hidden by an old choice.
Types and severity
Seven types, ordered by what they block for the team, from most to least critical: stuck review loop (a ticket can no longer move), gate to present (the team waits for your decision), raised question (a story waits for a business rule), ADR deviating from the stack (blocks G2 or the sprint it touches), high-impact open point, open reservation, process change (nothing is blocked). The colour follows this scale, from dark red to a cool grey; the label always spells out the type. Rows are sorted by severity, then from the oldest wait to the most recent; the filter chips follow the same order. Redder means more serious, as for defect severity.
Empty state
Without a hotspot, the list gives way to "No hotspot". A line under the list names the empty types as soon as there are some, so that an absence reads as checked, not forgotten.
Why this format
It is the reason to open the page: the section comes right after the Overview, before the figures. What only waits for the team (a ticket in progress, a question still open with the PO) is not listed.
tpl.dashboard.info.indicators:
<dt>What it is for</dt><dd>Measure progress and quality in four cards, without opening the board.</dd>
          <dt>What it shows</dt><dd>From the widest to the closest: stories delivered out of the total of all releases, then out of the current release (total of the story map, delivered according to the signed acceptance reports), then the tickets of the current sprint by status; open defects, one counter per severity (greyed at zero) and one row per defect.</dd>
          <dt>Why this format</dt><dd>Every number can be recounted in a file: stories accepted in the reports, tickets and defects in the front matter of the board. The detail stays in the sprint page and the campaign; here, only the order of magnitude and what should worry.</dd>
          <dt>Reading</dt><dd>Hovering or focusing a gauge segment gives its number. A story counts as delivered when a signed acceptance report accepts it, with or without reservations.</dd>
tpl.dashboard.info.latest-events:
What it is for
Show what happened since the last visit, without reading the journal.
What it shows
The last five lines of the journal, most recent first; the button shows five more at each click. The page holds at most the last 50 lines, without the dispatch and report lines, which trace the work of the agents.
Why this format
The journal is the memory of the PO, one line per event: the page shows it as is, with the type of the line as a label, so that the original line can be found.
tpl.bl.title: Backlog
tpl.bl.info.summary:
What it is for
Show at a glance how many stories are at each step, for the whole project and for each release, before going into the detail by epic.
What it shows
One card for all releases, then one per release, in the order of the story map: stories delivered out of the total, a gauge by status, the count of each status present, the spread of sizes and the front share of the release.
Sources
The total and the release of each story come from the story map; the status, from the rule described in the Backlog section; the size and the front share, from the page of each story.
Front share
The average front share of the stories of the card, weighted by their size with the scale of the roadmap (Human values: XS 1, S 2, M 4, L 5, XL 8), rounded to the percent: an L story weighs more than an S story.
Reading
Hovering or focusing a gauge segment gives its status and number. A story counts as delivered when a signed acceptance report accepts it, with or without reservations: the same count as the steering page.
tpl.bl.info.backlog:
What it is for
See where each story stands, filed under its epic, with what is needed to decide: its release, its size, its front share, its status.
What it shows
A header per epic, in the order of their id: its id and title, without totals. Its stories below, by release (in the order of the story map) then by id. All rows are visible: at this backlog size, filters replace folding, and nothing hides a status. Counts are in the Summary.
Size and front
Read in the story page, tags size (XS to XL) and front (the share of the work on the front end, in %, the rest on the back end): the same source as the macro estimate of the roadmap. An XL story is split before entering a sprint, and before G1 for a release presented at G1. The bar shows both shares in two shades of the same weight; the numbers prevail.
Untitled column
What details the status: the acceptance report that accepted the story and its reservation RES-xx, the sprint that committed it, who approved it and when, an open question, a gap between sources (exclamation mark, leading to the Gaps between sources section).
Status of a story
A single scale, in the order of the flow:
  • To write: the story is in the story map, its page does not exist yet;
  • Written: its page exists, status draft;
  • Ready: its Definition of Ready is checked, status ready;
  • Approved: status validated; approved by the human at G1, or, written after G1, approved by the PO and shown to the human at the next G3;
  • In sprint N: committed to sprint N, according to its sprint page, status in-sprint;
  • Delivered: accepted in a signed acceptance report, with or without reservations, status done. The report prevails, as for the steering page.
A dropped story (status abandoned) stays at the end of its epic, struck through, and leaves the counts.
Filter
Two rows of chips, Release and Status, with their number of stories; a status absent from the backlog stays visible, greyed, to show the whole scale. Within a row, several chips add up; the two rows combine. An epic without a displayed story disappears with its header. The filter is not kept from one visit to the next.
Links
Each id leads to its page. A page not produced yet (a story to write) keeps its link, flagged as a warning by the deliverable check.
tpl.bl.info.gaps-between-sources:
<dt>What it is for</dt><dd>Show where two files of the project say different things about a story, so that the PO reconciles them before the next planning.</dd>
          <dt>What it shows</dt><dd>One row per gap, with the source kept by this page and the one that contradicts it. In the table, an exclamation mark on the row of the story leads here.</dd>
          <dt>Rules</dt><dd>Size and front share come from the story page, which the roadmap also reads; release and epic, from the story map; the delivered status, from a signed acceptance report. A value that contradicts the source kept is a gap, not a correction. In the table, the exclamation mark is in the untitled column of the story.</dd>
          <dt>Empty state</dt><dd>Without a gap, the list gives way to "No gap between the story map, the roadmap, the stories and the acceptance reports".</dd>
tpl.an.title: Workstream analyses
tpl.an.info.workstreams:
What it is for
See for each workstream the question asked, who handled it, where it stands, what it recommends, what it leaves open and what it changes elsewhere.
What it shows
One row per analysis page of docs/10-analysis/, except the big picture, whatever the phase or release it prepares: a single table. Workstreams in progress first, then the partly reported ones, then the done ones: what still needs work is on top. On a tie, the most recent date first.
Workstream
The title of the analysis, linked to its page, and under it the question of the workstream, taken from the lede of the analysis.
Author
AI when an agent of the team handled the workstream, else the name of the person who did; then the date of the page. Read in the meta of the analysis, aligned with its header.
Progress
Where the workstream stands, read in the meta of the analysis, aligned with the Workstream field of its header: in progress (one more pass is due), done, partly reported (timebox spent without a complete answer).
Status
Where the page stands, read in the meta of the analysis, aligned with the Status field of its header: draft, in-review, validated. Progress says whether the BA has finished, status whether the page passed its review and its gate.
For
The phase or release the workstream prepares, read in the meta of the analysis, aligned with the For field of its header, with the label of the columns of the steering page: P1 for a workstream opened from the big picture; P2, P3, MVP, R2… for a workstream opened after G1. The steering page shows a Workstream analyses card in each column that at least one workstream prepares.
Recommendation
The text of the Recommendation block of the analysis. The BA recommends, the PO decides: a recommendation is not a decision. A workstream in progress without a recommendation says so.
Still open
The questions Q-xxx of the Questions and assumptions section still open, linked to the questions page, then the number of assumptions. Nothing open: "Nothing".
Impacted deliverables
The deliverables of the first column of the Impacts on other deliverables section, linked, one per line. Section missing: "Not identified yet".
Filter
Four rows of chips in the order of the columns, Author (AI or person), Progress, Status and For, with their number of workstreams; an absent value stays visible, greyed, to show the whole scale. Within a row, several chips add up; rows combine; "All" clears its row. Without a result: a message says that nothing matches the filter. The filter is not kept from one visit to the next.
Sort
On a wide screen, a click on a header sorts the table on that column, a second click reverses it: Workstream by title, Author by date of the page, Progress and Status in the order of their scale, For in the order of the columns of the steering page, Still open by number of questions then of assumptions. Recommendation and Impacted deliverables do not sort. On load, and always on mobile where headers are hidden, the order described above.
Links
A page not produced yet keeps its link, flagged as a warning by the deliverable check.
Empty state
Without an analysis, the table gives way to "No workstream analysis: the big picture is not split into workstreams yet".
